'''Trifle''', also commonly known as sherry trifle, is a traditional layered [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] in many countries. It can be prepared with or without alcohol, and the nonalcoholic version is popular with children.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[wikipedia:Swiss roll|swiss roll]] or similar sponge cake
* 50–100 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] dry [[Cookbook:Sherry|sherry]]
* 1 packet/sachet fruit-flavoured [[Cookbook:Jelly|jelly]] (can be found under the brand names "Quick-Jel" or "Jell-O")
* 1 tin of [[Cookbook:Peach|peach]] segments
* [[Cookbook:Crème Anglaise|Custard]]
* Whipped double [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
* Hundreds and thousands, [[Cookbook:Sprinkles|sprinkles]], or other sweet topping (optional)

== Procedure == 
# [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] the Swiss roll approximately ¾-inch (2 cm) thick, and line the base of a Pyrex [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|casserole dish]] with it.
# Pour sherry over the swiss roll.
# Drain the peaches, keeping the juice/syrup aside and then arrange the peaches over the swiss roll.
# Prepare the jelly as per the instructions, you may wish to use the syrup from the peaches for this. Pour the jelly into the casserole dish and allow to set in the fridge.
# Make the custard, again as per the instructions (use fresh or powdered as opposed to canned). Allow this to cool to lukewarm, and pour into the casserole. Allow this to set in the fridge.
# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] the cream for the top of the trifle and spread it over the custard. Garnish with hundreds and thousands, sprinkles, or other cake decorations.
# Serve!
